_note: Quaki jumps: the questions on the signs, one pool per level. a[0] is right, the others are the lily pads that sink. r = the rule in one sentence (shown in Gentle mode after a mistake). src = where the question comes from (quaki-springt: written for this game). Answers ≤ 18 characters, questions ≤ 64. Each question has exactly one correct option among its answers (British English); written 2026-10-30 by the games run, see automation/reports/games.md.

A1.r: he, she, it + is: she is a teacher.
I + am: I am from Brazil.
we, you, they + are: we are hungry.

A1.q: I've got ___ apple in my bag.
A1.r: an before a vowel sound: an apple.
a before a consonant sound: a new car.
Bread is uncountable: some bread, not a bread.
at + a clock time: at 8 o'clock.
in + a month: in May.
on + a day: on Monday.

A1.q: I get up early ___ the morning.
A1.r: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening.
he, she, it: the verb takes -s – she lives.
I, you, we, they: no -s – they play.
he, she, it + doesn't + verb: he doesn't like.
Questions with you: Do you + verb?
What asks about a thing: What is your name?
Where asks about a place.

A1.q: This is Tom. ___ is my brother.
A1.r: A man or boy is he.
Before a noun: my, your, his, her, our, their.

A1.q: There ___ two chairs in the room.
A1.r: There are + plural: there are two chairs.
There is + one thing: there is a bank.
can + verb, never -s, never to: birds can fly.
child → children (irregular plural).
After s, x, ch, sh: add -es – boxes.
Orders and requests start with the base verb: Close the window.
twenty years old: years with -s after a number above one.
Before a noun: my book.
he, she, it + has: Tom has a dog.
or gives a choice: hot or cold?
How many + plural noun: how many brothers?

A1.q: I'm hungry, ___ I'm making a sandwich.
A1.r: so gives the result: I'm hungry, so I eat.

A2.q: I was cooking when the phone ___.
A2.r: ring → rang: the short action in the past simple.
did + base verb: Did you see?
never = not at any time: I've never been there.
yet at the end of negatives: I haven't finished yet.

A2.q: This bag is ___ than that one.
It's the ___ day of the year.

A2.r: going to + verb for a plan.

A2.q: We ___ going to the cinema tonight.
A2.r: we are + -ing for a plan: we are going.

A2.q: You ___ wear a seat belt. It's the law.
A2.r: must = it is necessary, there is a rule.

A2.q: You ___ smoke here. It's not allowed.

A2.r: How much + uncountable noun: how much milk?
since + a point in time: since 2019.
for + a length of time: for six years.

A2.q: If it rains, we ___ stay at home.
I took a taxi ___ the bus was late.
I usually ___ to work by bus.
Could you ___ me the salt, please?

B1.q: If I ___ more time, I'd learn Japanese.
B1.r: Unreal now: if + past simple, would + verb.
Passive past: was/were + past participle.
be used to + -ing: I'm used to getting up.
wish + past for now: I wish I were (or was) taller.

B1.q: This is the man ___ car was stolen.
B1.r: whose = his, her, their in a relative clause.
for + a length of time.

B1.q: You ___ have told me! I'd have helped.
B1.r: should have + participle: it was a good idea, but you didn't.
look forward to + -ing.
despite + noun or -ing, no of.

B1.q: He stopped ___ because it was bad for him.
B1.r: stop + -ing = not do it any more.
too + adjective + to: more than is good.

B1.q: The film was so ___ that I fell asleep.
B1.r: -ing describes the thing (boring film), -ed the feeling (I was bored).
Earlier past: had + past participle.

B1.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ miss the bus.
B1.r: unless = if not: unless you hurry, you will miss it.

B1.q: I don't know ___ he's coming or not.
B1.r: whether … or not for two possibilities.
suggest + -ing, not suggest to.
had better + base verb.
would rather + base verb.

B1.q: The more you practise, the ___ you get.
B1.r: the + comparative, the + comparative.

B1.q: He's the person ___ I told you about.
B1.r: who (or that) for people in a relative clause.

B2.q: If I'd known, I ___ have come.
B2.r: Unreal past: if + had + participle, would have + participle.

B2.q: Hardly ___ arrived when it started to rain.
B2.r: Hardly at the start: question word order – hardly had we.
Passive with a modal: must be + past participle.

B2.q: He is said ___ the richest man in town.
I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
B2.r: would rather + another person + past simple.

B2.q: Not only ___ late, but he forgot the tickets.
B2.r: Not only at the start: question word order – was he.

B2.q: She ___ have taken the train: her car is here.
B2.r: must have + participle: you are sure about the past.

B2.q: I object ___ being treated like a child.
No sooner had I sat down ___ the phone rang.
Little ___ she know what was coming.
B2.r: Little at the start: little did she know.

B2.q: The flat, ___ windows face the sea, is for sale.
B2.r: whose for things too: the flat whose windows …

C1.q: ___ the rain, the match went ahead.
C1.r: despite + noun; although + a full clause.

C1.q: Should you ___ any questions, call me.
C1.r: Should you + base verb = if you have.

C1.q: It was not until midnight ___ he came home.
So ___ was the noise that nobody slept.

C1.r: be believed + to have + participle for the past.
A What-clause takes a singular verb: what I need is …
Only then at the start: question word order.
the cost of which = whose cost.
would sooner + another person + past simple.

C1.q: Much ___ I admire him, I disagree.

C1.r: Seldom at the start: question word order.
Were she here = if she were here.

C1.q: Under no circumstances ___ open this door.
C1.r: Under no circumstances at the start: question word order.

C1.q: Having ___ the letter, she burst into tears.
C1.r: Having + past participle: first this, then that.

C1.q: There's no point ___ about it now.
___ it not been for you, I'd have failed.
C1.r: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for.
